messages:
akash: Heads-up — seeing a small but sustained spike of mixed Xid codes (13 / 79 / 48) on several eu-central A10 nodes since ~08:15 UTC. Error bursts line up with batch-encode tenant traffic. Anyone picked this up in telemetry?

infra-bot: Auto-alert: gpu-fleet-eucent-azb high XID error rate. New aggregate: 37 events in last 30m. Linked logs -> /logs/gpu/eu-central/1759456789/ (ephemeral).

maria: I’m pulling dmesg + NVML for the affected hosts now. Initial glance: Xid 13 and 48 co-occur on the same PCI slot occasionally, 79 shows up on long-running decode tasks.

sam: Can you paste a couple dmesg lines? also which kernel/driver? we recently rolled driver 535.86 on that region last week.

maria: Paste snippet: ```[  4873.122345] NVRM: Xid (13:00000000) GPU has fallen off the bus. PID 4321 (python)```
[  4873.122358] NVRM: Xid (48:00000000) Channel exception on channel 0x00000007.
[  4890.987654] NVRM: Xid (79:00000000) Fault during copy engine operation.```

akash: Batch-encode tenant is ~30% of eu-central traffic atm, small requests but lots of concurrent short sequences. Could be heat-related or PCI flapping from noisy neighbor. Temp sensors look fine from general telemetry.

olga: Recommending triage steps: 1) map Xid->workload by looking at process PIDs + container IDs at event times (maria), 2) run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTILIZATION` on suspect hosts (sam), 3) if same GPU shows repeated XIDs, mark for drain+replace (olga).

sam: Ran `nvidia-smi -q` on node gpu-euc-azb-12: ECC reports no correctable/uncorrectable counts, but util spikes and ECC error counters reset after driver reload. Command used: `ssh gpu-euc-azb-12 sudo systemctl restart nvidia-drm` — saw a temporary drop in Xid events.

maria: Mapped a few PIDs -> containers: `kubectl logs` shows the batch-encode client using a pinned model variant with long KV cache in some pods; those processes had repeated GPU faults right before container restarted.

akash: Hypothesis: a combination of continuous small sequences producing many context-switched kernels + a recent driver/kernel combo causing sporadic channel exceptions. Could be a memory access timing issue showing as different Xid codes depending on stage.

sam: Also noticed one host has slightly older firmware on the GPU (FW 2.3 -> fleet baseline 2.5). Opening a firmware mismatch ticket: TKT-1458.

olga: Ops plan for next 2 hours: 1) throttle batch-encode concurrency in eu-central to 60% (rate-limit) 2) proactively drain GPUs with >5 Xid events in last 1h (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) 3) collect nv-host logs and escalate to HW if drains don’t stop events.

maria: Running a quick canary: throttled tenant, restarted driver on two nodes, removed one host from rotation (drain started). I’ll push the log bundle to /shared/infra/gpu-triage/1759456789.tar.gz

infra-bot: Action recorded: throttle applied to tenant batch-encode (policy id: policy-euc-07). Drains started on nodes: gpu-euc-azb-12, gpu-euc-azb-19.

akash: If drains stop Xid noise, we’ll mark as flaky card / replace. If not, escalate to driver or infra-level (firmware). Keep notes on whether Xid types change after driver reloads.

sam: Quick check: running `sudo dmesg | grep -i Xid | tail -n 20` on gpu-euc-azb-12 returns nothing after the restart (10m clean). I’m reintroducing one drained node back to pool after monitoring for 15m.

maria: Collected mapping: tenant IDs -> container IDs -> PIDs -> GPU IDs for the 08:10–08:40 window and added to the bundle.

olga: Postmortem actions to schedule: 1) add Xid-by-tenant alert with automatic rate-based throttling 2) nightly job to detect firmware drift vs fleet baseline 3) document drain playbook for mixed Xid bursts.

akash: Thanks all — keep updates here. If we still see 79 after firmware standardization, we’ll open HW ticket with NVML traces and kernel logs.

maria: Quick note: one replaced card returned clean for 48/13 but still saw 79 during heavy copy ops. Suggest we treat 79 separately (copy-engine/firmware/driver race).

olga: Agreed. Splitting followups: HW/replace for recurring 13/48, infra+driver/firmware for 79. I’ll create two tracking tickets and assign owners. :white_check_mark:
